A "bone of contention" is a specific issue, topic, or matter that causes disagreement or argument between two or more people (or groups). It is the central point around which a conflict or dispute revolves.

Think of it as the exact thing two sides are fighting about — not the fight itself, but the subject at the heart of it.

For example, if two siblings constantly argue about who gets to use the family car, the car is the bone of contention. If two countries are in a long-standing dispute over a piece of land, that land is the bone of contention.

The phrase is centuries old and paints a vivid, simple picture in your mind. Imagine two dogs fighting over a single bone. Both want it. Neither will let go. The bone is the one thing causing all the growling and snapping between them.

This image was borrowed to describe human arguments. Just like the dogs and their bone, when two people or groups are locked in disagreement, the "bone" is the specific issue they are both pulling at from opposite sides.

The word "contention" comes from the Latin word contentio, which means struggle, rivalry, or dispute. So "bone of contention" literally and figuratively means "the bone over which there is a struggle."

The phrase has been in use in the English language since at least the 16th century, and it has remained in everyday use ever since — a sign of how perfectly the image captures the idea.

Bone — represents the specific issue, topic, or object at the center of the conflict. It's not just any issue; it's the one thing both sides want to "own" or resolve in their favor.

Contention — means disagreement, dispute, or argument. If something is "in contention," it is being argued over or competed for.

Put them together: a bone of contention = the specific thing being argued over.
How It Is Used in a Sentence

This phrase is a noun phrase, which means it functions as a "thing" in a sentence — it can be the subject, object, or complement of a sentence.

It almost always appears with the article "a" or "the":

  • "The division of household chores has long been a bone of contention between the two roommates."
  • "Salary increases became the bone of contention at the negotiating table."
  • "Land ownership is a major bone of contention in that region."
  • "How to spend the holiday budget turned out to be a bone of contention at the family dinner."
  • "Data privacy remains a bone of contention between tech companies and governments."

You can also use modifiers like "major," "real," "long-standing," or "constant" before it to show how serious or persistent the disagreement is — for example, "a real bone of contention" or "a long-standing bone of contention."
Key Things to Understand About This Phrase

It is neutral. The phrase does not take sides. It doesn't tell you who is right or wrong. It simply identifies the point of disagreement. You can use it to describe a conflict even if you are not personally involved.

It implies persistence. A bone of contention is usually not a one-off, five-second argument. It tends to suggest an issue that has caused repeated or ongoing conflict — something that keeps coming up and doesn't get resolved easily.

It can be used in any scale of conflict — from small personal disagreements (two friends arguing about money) to large political or international disputes (two nations disagreeing over a policy or territory).

It is both formal and informal. You can use this phrase in casual everyday conversation, in a professional email, in a news article, or in an academic essay. It fits all contexts naturally.
Don't Confuse It With "A Bone to Pick"

A very common phrase that sounds similar but means something different is "I have a bone to pick with you."

This means: "I have a specific complaint or grievance I want to raise with you." It is more personal and one-sided — one person is dissatisfied and wants to confront another.

A bone of contention, on the other hand, is the shared issue that both sides are disagreeing about. It's the subject of a two-way (or multi-way) dispute, not just one person's complaint.

Think of it this way: you might "have a bone to pick" with your colleague about something, and that something is the "bone of contention" between you two.

Several other phrases and words convey a similar meaning, and knowing them will help you recognize the idea when it appears in different forms:

"Point of contention" — essentially the same meaning as "bone of contention." Both are widely used, and you can often swap one for the other.

"Sticking point" — an issue that prevents two sides from reaching an agreement, often used in negotiations.

"Matter of dispute" or "subject of dispute" — more formal ways of saying the same thing.

"Apple of discord" — a more literary phrase borrowed from Greek mythology. In the story, a golden apple caused a fierce argument among goddesses, ultimately leading to the Trojan War. Like "bone of contention," it refers to something that sparks conflict, but "apple of discord" sounds more dramatic and literary.

"Contentious issue" — an adjective form; a "contentious issue" is an issue that causes contention, which is essentially the same idea from a different angle.
A Quick Summary to Lock It In

A bone of contention is the specific subject, issue, or matter that lies at the heart of a disagreement between people or groups. The image is simple: two dogs fighting over one bone. The bone is what they're fighting over, not the fight itself. In human terms, whenever two sides are arguing, whatever they're arguing about is the bone of contention. It's a neutral, versatile, and timeless phrase used across all kinds of contexts — personal, professional, and political — to point clearly to the root cause of a conflict.
